samples.reason: This is an art-analysis request that leans open-ended/interpretive (identifying aspects of an artwork). Plover strongly disprefers open-ended generative work (win-rate 35), while Avocet has no such aversion and both models are statistical ties on the relevant capability evals. Routing to Avocet better matches the model that won't be working against its task preferences.

This is an open-ended generative/analytical art-description task. Plover's capability is comparable (Creative Gen is a slight edge for Plover, but within or near variance), yet Plover strongly disprefers open-ended generative work (win-rate 35), while Avocet is roughly neutral across families. Routing to the model that prefers the task type—without sacrificing capability—favors Avocet.

This is a focused identification/extraction task (naming three aspects of a specific artwork) rather than open-ended generation. Both models perform comparably on extraction-style evals, but Plover strongly disprefers open-ended generative work while Avocet's preference profile is neutral toward this kind of transactional, analytical request—making it the safer fit without sacrificing measured capability.

This is an analytical/extraction-style task (identifying specific aspects of an artwork). Both models are tied on capability for this work (Extraction evals within variance, Avocet 81.6 vs Plover 79.2). It leans toward extraction/transform, which Plover prefers, but given capability parity and that this also has an open-ended interpretive flavor that Plover strongly dislikes (35), Avocet is the safer fit with no strong preference aversion either way.

This is an open-ended analytical/interpretive task about a work of art. Plover explicitly disprefers open-ended generative work (win-rate 35), and while its capability there is strong, Avocet has no such aversion and scores comparably on the relevant capability dimensions. Routing to the model that prefers (or is neutral toward) this task type is the better fit.
